title: Diff signal sampling notes and micro-refactor roadmap
content:
Context
---
Personal notes on how I want to triage diffs that touch the runtime hot path (kv-cache, batching, kernel-selection). Mostly a lightweight checklist + a few tiny refactors I want to prototype. Leaving a lot of open questions here; this is a working brain dump.

Goals
- Make PR triage faster for low-latency bits: catch subtle perf regressions before they land.
- Reduce reviewer burden by standardizing a minimal signal set we ask for on each PR.
- Have small, reversible refactors that make reasoning about perf easier.

Quick heuristic: "fast-sanity" signals to ask for on every PR touching runtime core:
1) Microbenchmark snippet (if touching loop / batching): synthetic 1, 8, 32 token runs; median of 5 runs.
2) Unit test coverage: ensure added logic has focused unit tests for edge branches (e.g., cache miss path).
3) Change summary line at top of PR: why this might affect latency/cost.
4) Backwards compatibility note (config flags, env var changes).
5) If changing kernel selection heuristics, add a small table of expected model/seq thresholds.

Checklist (PR triage flow)
- Sanity: does CI include the perf smoke job? If not, ask author to re-run locally and paste numbers.
- Measure: Author should paste the 5-run median throughput and p95 latency for a minimal scenario. If not possible, mark as "needs perf" and request quick bench.
- Safety net: Is there a fallback path / feature-flag? If no, flag for extra reviewer.
- Complexity: if the diff > 200 LOC in runtime, request high-level diagram and a small integration test.

Lightweight perf smoke script (ask authors to run):
- tools/mini-bench --model small-llama --seq 8 --batch 1 --n 100
- tools/mini-bench --model small-llama --seq 32 --batch 8 --n 50
Paste median/95 numbers into PR description.

Common subtle failure modes I keep seeing
- Hidden allocations in hot loop (string concat, fmt.Sprintf) -> pin to bytes.Buffer or pre-allocated slice.
- Unnecessary interface boxing (interface{} used in inner loop).
- Synchronous file/metrics flush in hot path (defer + file write per request).
- Kernel path misselection for short sequences due to rounding thresholds.

Micro-refactor ideas (cheap, high-signal)
1) Introduce a small runtime/fasttype package (100 LOC) that ships type-hints for inner loops. Benefit: reduce interface boxing and simplify benching. Risk: minimal, compile-time only.
2) Move string-concats in token-serialization into a reusable pool-backed builder. Start with 1 caller (response serializer) and measure.
3) Replace ad-hoc feature flag checks with a single decision struct passed into hot loops (less branching when reading feature flags).
4) Extract kernel-selection thresholds into a JSON-ish table under configs/ with unit tests that validate selection for representative models.

Prioritized follow-ups (small PRs)
- PF-1 (P1): Add mini-bench integration to CI as an optional smoke job (fails only on regression >10%). Put behind a nightly gate first. Owner: me.
- PF-2 (P2): Prototype runtime/fasttype and convert one hot-loop. Target: < 150 LOC change, keep feature-flagged. Owner: Maya.
- PF-3 (P2): Add a test harness that runs 3 sequences (1/8/32) across cpu/gpu images for our core ci image. Owner: Evan.

Notes-to-self / review language snippets to paste into PRs
- "This change affects the batching loop in X. I ran the mini-bench (command + results) and saw no >5% regression on median throughput. See bench output."
- "This adds a new selection path. Backstop: if .selectKernel returns nil we fall back to legacy path; documented in config.md."

Open questions / TODOs
- Can we get the CI infra team to add a lightweight perf VM that can run mini-bench with GPUs? Ticket: INF-2317 (linked).
- How much noise do we tolerate from GPU warm-up? Need to formalize bench protocol (discard first 3 runs?)
- Are there any legal/privacy concerns if mini-bench uploads traces? We should mute traces by default.

Small code snippet to paste into PR (perf guard macro style)
```
// fast-guard: measure-only (no-op in prod)
if env.Bool("ENABLE_MINI_BENCH") {
  // run a quick microbench and log med/p95
  go runMiniBench()
}
```

Reviewer heuristics (when I'm the reviewer)
- If author can't run bench locally, ask them to at least add a simple unit test covering the new branch.
- Prefer many small PRs vs one big change for runtime code. If a large change is unavoidable, ask for a design doc.
- Don't accept changes that increase allocation churn without measurable benefit.

References / examples I liked
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4876 (good bench snippet in description)
- Confluence draft: DEV-coverage-signals (linked above)

Closing notes
- Keep this doc minimal and copy snippets into a reusable review template in the repo (CONTRIBUTING.md).
- When PF-1 is live, iterate on the bench thresholds. Start conservative (10% regression) then relax if we see false positives.

Unresolved (write down for later)
- How to encode multi-model routing tests cheaply? (cheap = under 5 minutes per run)
- Should we require authors to run a smoke for their actual model config, or is a canonical small model ok?

-- Rohan
